headline: Recommended $320,000 for Gore estate window restoration, $85,000 for 20 Felton Street, and $50,768 for First Parish steeple.
summary: The original steeple contractor never started work, and the other bids were higher, so First Parish asked for more money. A bid from a Community Day Center board member's company was dropped because of a conflict of interest. The Gore estate window request passed 6-1, and the group also reappointed its officers and closed four old accounts.
decisions: Approved minutes of the May 12, 2026 meeting, with one abstention.
Recommended $50,768 to City Council for First Parish Church steeple preservation and restoration, 8-0 roll call.
Recommended $85,000 to City Council for exterior restoration of 20 Felton Street, 7-0 with one member absent.
Recommended $320,000 to City Council for window restoration on the south side of the Gore estate, 6-1 vote.
Reappointed Justin Barrett as chair, Erika Oliver Jerram as vice chair and Julie Toole as clerk, unanimously.
Closed four old open accounts, unanimously.

$85,000 for exterior restoration of 20 Felton Street

plain_text:
1 
Approved 11-17-2026 
 
Community Preservation Committee 
Meeting Minutes 
September 22, 2026 
 
  
1.  Call to Order 
Meeting called to order at 7:02 p.m. by Chair Justin Barrett.  This meeting was held via Zoom and was 
recorded for future viewing on The Waltham Channel. 
2.  Roll Call 
Present: Chair Justin Barrett, Vice Chair Erika Oliver Jerram (arrived at 7:03 p.m.), Tom Creonte, Frank 
Fitzgerald, Bob LeBlanc, Loretta McClary, Amanda Thibodeau, Sean Wilson 
Absent: None 
 
3.  Meeting Minutes 
Motion made by Mr. LeBlanc to approve the meeting minutes of May 12, 2026, seconded by Mr. Fitzgerald.  
Mr. Wilson abstained from voting because he did not attend that meeting.  All in favor.  Motion passed. 
4.  New Business  
A.  Public Meeting 
1. First Parish Church Steeple Preservation and Restoration Application Additional Funding 
Request ($50,768) 
Walter Beebe Center, Property Commissioner, First Parish, noted that they applied for a grant last fall to 
preserve their steeple.  Their selected bidder, American Steeple, did not start the work and has ghosted 
them since this past May. The other two quotes they received were substantially higher, therefore the 
additional funding request.  Mr. Barrett stated that they were approved a year ago (Oct. 2025) for $77,250 
and are now requesting an additional $50,768.  Ms. McClary asked if the quotes are from last year or if they 
have been updated.  Mr. Beebe Center confirmed they are current quotes.   Mr. Fitzgerald asked if there has 
been a structural assessment of the steeple.  Mr. Beebe Center replied that they believe it is stable and good 
for another century.  It was built in 1933 and is constructed of steel and wood.  Mr. LeBlanc asked if they had 
a signed contract with the original vendor.  Mr. Beebe Center said they had a signed proposal. There was an 
agreement to move forward, but they have been incommunicative with him.  Mr. LeBlanc noted how low the 
quote was compared to the other two.  Mr. Beebe Center chose them because of their very strong positive 
references and the lower quote made them the clear choice.  Mr. LeBlanc asked where the new vendor is 
from.  Mr. Beebe Center replied that they (Painter’s Pride Inc.) are out of Natick, and they have been 
restoring steeples for over 20 years. 
 
Motion made by Ms. Oliver Jerram to recommend to the City Council the First Parish Church application for 
$50,768.  Motion seconded by Ms. McClary.
2 
Approved 11-17-2026 
Roll call vote:  Justin Barrett (yes), Erica Oliver Jerram (yes), Tom Creonte (yes), Frank Fitzgerald (yes), Bob 
LeBlanc (yes), Loretta McClary (yes), Amanda Thibodeau (yes), Sean Wilson (yes) 
All in favor.  Motion passed.    
 
Ms. McClary left the meeting (7:15 p.m.). 
 
2. Community Day Center 20 Felton Street Exterior Restoration Application ($104,600) 
Chloe-Rose Crouch, Executive Director of Community Day Center, stated that they offer shelter and support 
services for individuals experiencing homelessness in Waltham.  The two buildings that they own – 16 Felton 
and 20 Felton – is where they run all of their operations.  At 16 Felton St. they do their drop-in day services.  
At 20 Felton St., the building is in serious disrepair of the exterior.  They hold their emergency night program 
from Dec. 1st through April 15th every year, which provides homeless individuals a place to stay during the 
cold months.  Also at this building, they have their free clothing store.  Guests can “shop” for free for 
essentials they need including clothing and hygiene items.  Their case management program is also held 
there.  The building was built in the late 1800s and it originally was a beef manufacturing and storage facility.  
All of the siding and windows need to be replaced.  20 Felton St. abuts right up to 22 Felton St. leaving very 
little space between the buildings.  She is requesting funding to restore the three walls that are facing the 
elements and are visible from the street.  The Historical Commission requested that she revise the estimates 
to include the fourth side.  She received them too late for the CPC’s review, therefore she is asking for 
funding to restore the initial three sides.  Mr. Barrett pointed out that Mike Columba is on their board of 
directors, he previously owned the building, and his company provided one of the quotes.  He said that this is 
a huge conflict of interest and they cannot use his bid.  Mr. Barrett opened up questions from the 
committee.  Mr. Fitzgerald agreed with the conflict.  Ms. Crouch included Mr. Columba’s bid because at the 
time, she was struggling to hear back from contractors.  Mr. Barrett asked if the Historical Commission 
recommended which type of materials should be used.  Ms. Crouch said they suggested she speak with the 
CPC then the commission will work with the budget.  Mr. Creonte asked how many people they place in the 
winter at night.  Ms. Crouch replied that their maximum capacity is 20 people plus 2 staff members.  Their 
free store sees ~350 individuals a year, and their case management program has ~120 active clients.  Mr. 
LeBlanc asked if it has been determined that the fourth side of the building absolutely needs to be restored.  
Mr. Barrett responded that the Historical Commission would like it done.  There isn’t a lot of space to access 
the area.  Since the original quotes did not include the fourth side and the quotes came in today for that side, 
the CDC will need to come back to request additional funding.  Mr. LeBlanc asked if the contractors are able 
to start work this fall/winter.  Ms. Crouch replied that they are willing to start as soon as they are allowed.  
After some discussion on the cost of the quotes (and disqualifying Columba’s), the amount the CPC agreed to 
recommend to City Council is $85,000.  Mr. Creonte asked if the CDC has any money to put towards the 
project.  Ms. Crouch replied that they did fundraise and have $15k to put towards it.  Ms. Oliver Jerram 
commented that she is fine with the hardy board for the siding, but would like to make a plea for wood 
windows.  The committee agreed that the Waltham Historical Commission be involved with the decision of 
the materials for both the windows and siding. 
 
Motion made by Ms. Oliver Jerram to recommend to the City Council $85,000 for the exterior restoration of 
20 Felton Street, seconded by Ms. Thibodeau.   
Roll call vote: Justin Barrett (yes), Erika Oliver Jerram (yes), Tom Creonte (yes), Frank Fitzgerald (yes), Bob 
LeBlanc (yes), Loretta McClary (absent), Amanda Thibodeau (yes), Sean Wilson (yes) 
All in favor.  Motion passed.
3 
Approved 11-17-2026 
3. Gore Place Window Restoration Application ($350,000) 
Gavin Kleespies, Executive Director of Gore Place, stated that they were approved for CPA funding for design 
services to evaluate the condition of their south-facing windows.  They received two bids to restore the 
windows.  Window Woman of New England would remove the sashes and restoring them off-site, but they 
do not work on the framing.  GGB Custom Builders was a higher bid but they will do the carpentry of the 
framing.  Mr. Kleespies has worked with GGB in the past and he has been very pleased with their work.  Mr. 
Barrett asked for clarification re: the amount Gore Place is requesting vs. what the highest bid is (which 
includes a 10% contingency).  Mr. LeBlanc asked if they were able to get a bid from another company that is 
comparable to GGB’s bid.  They did not.  Mr. LeBlanc asked how many windows need restoration.  Mr. Clark, 
who was also in attendance for Gore Place, stated that 43 windows would be restored.  Mr. Creonte asked if 
Gore Place has any of their own funds for the project.  Mr. Kleespies replied that they most likely would be 
able to absorb additional unforeseen costs ($20k - $30k).  Mr. LeBlanc asked when work would start.  Mr. 
Kleespies stated that work could begin this winter. 
 
Motion made by Ms. Oliver Jerram to recommend to the City Council the window restoration of the south 
side of the Gore estate for $320,000.  Motion seconded by Mr. LeBlanc.   
Roll call vote: Mr. Barrett (yes), Ms. Oliver Jerram (yes), Mr. Creonte (no), Mr. Fitzgerald (yes), Mr. LeBlanc 
(yes), Ms. McClary (absent), Ms. Thibodeau (yes), Mr. Wilson (yes) 
Majority in favor.  Motion passed.   
 
B. Election of Officers 
Motion made by Mr. LeBlanc to reappoint Justin Barrett as Chair, Erika Oliver Jerram as Vice Chair and Julie 
Toole as Clerk of the CPC.  Seconded by Ms. Thibodeau.  All in favor.  Motion passed. 
  
C. Advertising 
Mr. Barrett noted that Ms. McClary mentioned that the Nantucket CPC advertises for applications in a local 
newspaper.  He isn’t sure if Waltham’s CPC needs to advertise since we get a good amount of applications 
throughout the year.  Ms. Oliver Jerram doesn’t see a need to solicit for applications.  Mr. LeBlanc suggested 
advertising on the local cable channel (WCAC.org) as a public service announcement.  Mr. Barrett will set it 
up. 
 
D.  Old Open Accounts 
Julie listed four old open accounts: Wellington House interior (2013), stone walls survey (2017), conservation 
land stewardship plan at Paine Estate (2019), and 56 Chestnut Street building improvements design services 
(2021) that haven’t had any activity on them in several years.  The Auditing Department notified the CPC that 
applicants should spend the money and accounts should be closed within three years of being approved.  
Mr. Barrett stated that Julie reached out to the Community Preservation Coalition to inquire if this written is 
in the CPA statute and was told it is not, but it is up to the city or town to decide on the duration of open 
accounts.  
 
Motion made by Mr. Creonte to close the four old accounts, seconded by Ms. Oliver Jerram.  All in favor. 
Motion passed. 
 
E.  Current CPA Balances 
Mr. Barrett gave an update on each of the account balances:  Open Space ($1,172,795.96), Historical 
($581,512.30), Housing ($0.00), and Undesignated ($4,288.68).
4 
Approved 11-17-2026 
5.  Announcements/Correspondence 
A.  Next meeting:  November 17, 2026 
 
6.  Adjourn 
Motion made by Mr. LeBlanc to adjourn, seconded by Ms. Oliver Jerram.  All in favor.   
Motion passed.  Meeting adjourned at 8:14 p.m.
